correctness.rationale: With \(q_t=\lambda\alpha_t\), the sign of consecutive scalar gradients gives exactly the multiplicative factors \(1+\beta\) for \(q_t<1\) and \(1-\beta\) for \(q_t>1\), matching the primary quadratic analysis after the normalization \(\lambda=2a\). Repeated multiplication enters \([1-\beta,1+\beta]\); there \(|1-q_t|\le\beta\), so \(|x_{t+1}|\le\beta|x_t|\). Put \(A=\log(1+\beta)\), \(C=-\log(1-\beta)\), and reduce \(\log q+C\) modulo \(A+C\); both branches become addition by \(A\). Standard circle-rotation dynamics then gives exact period equal to the denominator of rational \(A/(A+C)\), and dense orbits when it is irrational. The bundled verifier checks band entry, the conjugacy identity, a period-three example, dense-bin behavior, and contraction; these are corroborative of the exact proof.

originality.rationale: The 2017 Oxford thesis already derives the same multiplicative rule on one-dimensional quadratics, gives the three learning-rate regimes, proves eventual trapping in the identical \((1-\beta,1+\beta)\)-scaled interval, and notes geometric contraction there. After that published analysis, passing to logarithms turns the two multiplicative branches into a translation modulo \(\log((1+\beta)/(1-\beta))\); rational-periodic versus irrational-dense behavior is the standard circle-rotation classification. The final claim is therefore an implication-level dynamical corollary of the thesis rather than an uncovered scalar-quadratic theorem.

value.rationale: The rotation viewpoint gives a clean explanation of why the optimization variable can converge while the adaptive learning rate is periodic or dense, and it yields exact phase behavior for every \(\beta\). This is a useful structural interpretation, but it cannot pass acceptance because the underlying theorem is already implication-level covered.
residual_risks: The result is restricted to a scalar quadratic and does not establish analogous quasiperiodicity in higher dimensions.

final_claim: On the one-dimensional quadratic \(f(x)=\lambda x^2/2\), normalized multiplicative Hypergradient Descent with \(0<\beta<1\) has normalized learning-rate dynamics \(q_{t+1}=(1+\beta)q_t\) below \(1\) and \((1-\beta)q_t\) above \(1\); every nonresonant orbit eventually lies in \([1-\beta,1+\beta]\), where its logarithm is conjugate to a circle rotation of angle \(\theta=\log(1+\beta)/\log((1+\beta)/(1-\beta))\). Thus rational \(\theta\) gives exact periodic learning rates and irrational \(\theta\) gives dense nonconvergent learning rates, while the iterates still contract geometrically.
limitations: The theorem is for the scalar quadratic and the normalized multiplicative variant.
Resonant orbits that hit the exact optimal learning rate terminate at the minimizer and are excluded from the rotation classification.
